To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed framework can be used for skill synthesis of a robotic hand.

(1) humans are capable of learning to control a robotic arm and hand with their own body, (2) this control is robust and generalizes to new situations, and (3) this control can be used to design controllers for the robot.

a) a human can learn to control a robotic hand as if it were a part of his body, b) the human can learn to use the robot as a new limb to manipulate two objects in parallel and c) the dexterity exhibited with the new limb can be used to design a robot skill.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How to design controllers for robots by exploiting human expertise in a novel way?
the design of a novel robotic skill acquisition paradigm that can be used in the design of controllers for robotic manipulators.
the design and validation of an experimental setup that allows a person to control a robotic platform as if it was an external body part.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we propose a new paradigm for the design of robotic skills, which is based on the human capacity to acquire new motor tasks effortlessly and then to transfer the acquired knowledge to a robotic platform.
the framework proposed in this work is a novel approach for skill synthesis that can be used for the design of controllers that are effective for novel tasks.
the proposed framework allows for a fast, efficient, and effective skill synthesis for robots.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach for robot skill synthesis that can be used to derive a controller for the robotic hand that is as effective as that obtained by extensive human practice.
we are able to train a robot to perform a complex task in less than 10 min.

we show that it is possible to train a human to control a complex robotic hand with a set of simple instructions and a set of examples of the task, and that the resulting control policy can be used as the controller for the robotic system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed framework can be used to synthesize controllers with a high level of dexterity for a wide range of tasks, even if the robot is not equipped with sensors.
the robot can be trained to perform a task with a high degree of success by means of a few demonstrations and a large amount of practice.
, by means of a simple human training protocol, the human capacity to control a novel robotic platform can be leveraged for designing controllers that are effective in the real world.
